subject: german
title: Places in Town: Die Stadt
welcome_lead: Learn the essential places — bakery, post office, station, park — that fill every GCSE town description.
meta_desc: GCSE German town vocab: shops, public buildings and places with correct articles.
final_note: Don't just list places — say what you can do there: 'Im Park kann man spazieren gehen.'

concepts.def: Bakery — feminine, sells Brot and Brötchen.
Train station — masculine; Hauptbahnhof = main station.
Cinema — neuter; ins Kino gehen = to go to the cinema.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Most -ei feminine words: die Bäckerei, die Metzgerei.

Most -hof and -markt are masculine: der Bahnhof, der Supermarkt.

Foreign loanwords often neuter: das Kino, das Café, das Hotel.

Es gibt = there is / there are. It is followed by the accusative.

Examples:

  • In meiner Stadt gibt es einen Bahnhof. (m, einen)
  • Es gibt eine Bäckerei. (f, eine)
  • Es gibt ein Kino. (n, ein)
  • Es gibt viele Geschäfte. (pl)

walkthroughs.h2: Going to Places: ins / zum / zur
walkthroughs.body_html:
To say 'to the' for going somewhere:

  • ins Kino (n) — to the cinema
  • zum Bahnhof (m) — to the station
  • zur Post (f) — to the post office

Pattern: Ich gehe ins Kino / zum Bahnhof / zur Post.

In 'Heute gehe ich ins Kino', why does 'gehe' come second?
options: Heute is always followed by a verb.
German is a V2 language - the conjugated verb is the second element in main clauses.
